component.name: VibeSuperTonic
component.summary: Reads selected text aloud in a natural voice that runs on your computer

description.p: Select text in any application and press a key: VibeSuperTonic reads it aloud in a neural voice. Speech is generated on your own machine, so nothing you read is sent anywhere.
It is also a Speech Dispatcher voice, so Orca and other programs that speak on Linux can use the same voices.

ul.li: Two engines: Supertonic, and Piper with 65 voices in 35 languages
Global hotkeys: Ctrl+` reads the selection, Ctrl+~ stops
A window that follows along as it reads, with speed, voice and pronunciation controls

Works on X11, and on Wayland with KDE Plasma. On GNOME's Wayland session the hotkey cannot read the selection, because GNOME does not offer the protocol that allows it; the screen reader voices work everywhere
Optional GPU acceleration, falling back to the CPU on its own

description.p: The voice models are downloaded on first run, from Hugging Face, after you accept their licence. Connecting the hotkeys and the screen reader is one command in a terminal, which the application shows you.

screenshot.caption: Reading the selection aloud, highlighting each word
Downloading voices, with each voice's licence shown first
Engine, voice, speed and quality, for all voices or just one

description.p: First release as a snap and a Flatpak, so it can be installed from the Ubuntu App Center and from KDE Discover.

ul.li: Models and settings are kept in the sandbox's own folder and survive updates
The hotkeys and the screen reader voice are connected with one command, which the Status tab shows
Installing the screen reader voice now undoes itself if any other voice stops answering afterwards, and it no longer waits forever on a stuck Speech Dispatcher
The window opens from the tray again after you log out and back in
Export to MP3, AAC and FLAC works inside the sandbox, with its own small ffmpeg
